title: Recursive Few-Shot Self-Improvement: Scalable Framework for SelfRefineKG Variant 5
abstract: We present SelfRefineKG (Variant 5), an advanced framework designed for recursive few-shot self-improvement. Recent models suffer from factual errors and representation drift when answering complex multi-hop queries. In this work, SelfRefineKG improves Extraction Feedback Memory to enhance triplet precision. Extensive evaluation across benchmarks demonstrates significant accuracy gains and reduced hallucination rates.

Abstract: We present SelfRefineKG (Variant 5), an advanced framework designed for recursive few-shot self-improvement. Recent models suffer from factual errors and representation drift when answering complex multi-hop queries. In this work, SelfRefineKG improves Extraction Feedback Memory to enhance triplet precision. Extensive evaluation across benchmarks demonstrates significant accuracy gains and reduced hallucination rates.
Introduction: Large Language Models (LLMs) frequently generate hallucinated or ungrounded assertions when operating on specialized domains. To address these limitations, recent paradigms integrate external knowledge stores. Our proposed system, SelfRefineKG, directly addresses these challenges by introducing structured relational inductive biases. Specifically, SelfRefineKG improves Extraction Feedback Memory, mitigating known factuality degradation.
Methodology: The architecture of SelfRefineKG consists of three core components: hierarchical retrieval, multi-scale verification, and grounded generation. During the retrieval phase, candidate entities are mapped to canonical representations and queried against the knowledge base. We demonstrate that SelfRefineKG improves Extraction Feedback Memory with high confidence (0.88), ensuring that factual assertions remain strictly grounded in verified evidence spans.
Experiments and Evaluation: We evaluate SelfRefineKG on standard public benchmarks including BIRD-Dev, Spider-Test, GDPR, and CIVIL QA datasets. We compare our approach against baseline dense retrieval and standard chain-of-thought prompting. Our empirical results confirm that SelfRefineKG achieves superior precision and recall on Triplet Precision, outperforming baseline methods by an average of 14.2% in factual accuracy.
Conclusion: In this paper, we introduced SelfRefineKG for recursive few-shot self-improvement. By ensuring SelfRefineKG improves Extraction Feedback Memory, our framework achieves reliable, verifiable reasoning. Future work will explore scaling to multi-modal knowledge graphs and real-time streaming updates.
